validity.recommendation: Fix endpoint direction/labels: Start = Akkas (Okaz) gas field, End = Akkas (Akaz) gas power station (Al-Qaim district, Anbar). GEM currently records the field as the END (EndLocation='Okaz') with Start blank, which is backwards — the field is the gas SOURCE and the power station is the destination.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — CONFIRMED (high). This is a real, operating dry-gas line. Multiple independent sources place it: the Iraqi Economists PDF the sheet already cites (Al-Jibawi 2025) states 'In March 2023, SCOP announced its completion of a 16-inch dry gas pipeline from the Akkas gas field to the Akkas power station in Al-Anbar Province. The pipeline extends for 30 km with a capacity of 75 MMSCFD'; attaqa.net (Oct 2025) independently notes the field 'has ... a pipe transporting gas to the Akkas power station' (أنبوب لنقل الغاز إلى محطة كهرباء عكاس); Iraqi/Arab press (Sputnik Arabic, Economy News — the latter a wiki citation) report the Oil Minister announcing start of Akkas gas production at 60 MMcf/d in March 2023. CLASSIFICATION — CONFIRMED. It is a dedicated gas-transmission line from field to power station (Al-Jibawi labels its type 'Dry gas'); not an oil/NGL line (no match to any GulfPub Iraq crude line), not gathering/plant-internal. DUPLICATE — NONE on the roster. Distinct from the separate, larger, NOT-yet-built Akkas→Anbar power station line (26″/26″/24″, three sections Akkas→T1→K3→Anbar power station near Hit) that Al-Jibawi lists as planned — do not conflate the two. Also distinct from the GEM 'Akkas Gas Field' entity (a field, not a pipeline). ATTRIBUTION — operator نفط الوسط = Midland Oil Company (MdOC) CONFIRMED independently (iraq-businessnews, Iraq Oil Report, Zawya, iraqinews all name state-owned Midland Oil Company as the field operator that brought Akkas online March 2023); owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is defensible (MdOC is a state company under the MoO). Province Anbar CONFIRMED; FuelSource 'Okaz field' (= Akkas field) CONFIRMED. THE ONE ATTRIBUTION DEFECT is the Location endpoints: GEM stored EndLocation='Okaz' (the field, i.e. the source) and left Start blank; the real corridor is field → power station, so the labels are reversed/incomplete. Correct to Start=Akkas gas field, End=Akkas gas power station.

validity.recommendation: Keep 30 km / 16″ / 75 MMcf/d but flag as thinly corroborated: the ONLY source stating all three specs is the Al-Jibawi PDF (the sheet's own citation). Independent press consistently reports 60 MMcf/d as the throughput, and one 2022 pre-construction source gave 35 km. Treat Capacity=75 as design capacity, not verified flow.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC review. Length 30 km: stated by Al-Jibawi (30 km) and the iraq-businessnews production article (a '30-kilometre pipeline'); however one earlier (Aug 2022 'Work Begins') source gave 35 km as a pre-construction estimate. 30 km is the as-completed figure and is acceptable. Diameter 16″: sourced ONLY to Al-Jibawi ('16-inch dry gas pipeline'); no independent source I could token-verify restates the diameter — single-source (medium). Capacity 75 MMcf/d: sourced ONLY to Al-Jibawi (pipeline 'capacity of 75 MMSCFD'). Every other source — Sputnik Arabic, Economy News, Al Mayadeen, Iraq Business News — reports 60 MMcf/d as the March-2023 production/investment rate, and attaqa says the field's separation station is designed for ~50 MMcf/d. So 75 is a plausible pipeline DESIGN capacity that diverges from the 60 operational figure; it is not clearly wrong but rests on a single source. StartYear 2023 (March): CONFIRMED high (multiple). NOTE: the Al-Jibawi PDF is genuinely readable and contains all three specs verbatim, but scripts/url_verifier.py cannot token-match a compressed PDF, so it is not listed in proposed_refs here even though it is the sheet's legitimate cited source; the independent refs below corroborate existence/production/date but NOT the 16″/75 numbers.

fills.researcher_notes: Operating since March 2023: Oil Minister announced start of Akkas gas production/investment at 60 MMcf/d (Sputnik Arabic + Economy News, the latter a wiki citation). attaqa (2025) confirms the field is still producing and feeding the power station via the pipe.
Akkas is a dry-gas field; the line is a gas (dry gas) pipeline per Al-Jibawi and all Arabic press.
Dedicated field-to-power-station gas transport line (أنبوب لنقل الغاز إلى محطة كهرباء), i.e. transmission, not gathering/plant-internal. Al-Jibawi classes it 'Dry gas' transport.
Gas source is the Akkas (عكاز / Okaz) gas field in Anbar. 'Okaz' is GEM's transliteration of عكاز, more commonly romanized Akkas/Akkaz/Akkas.

ENDPOINT CORRECTION. GEM currently has EndLocation='Okaz' (the field) and Start blank — reversed. Real corridor: Start = Akkas (Okaz) gas field (source, ~30 km S of Al-Qaim, near the Syrian border), End = Akkas gas power station (near Al-Qaim, Anbar). attaqa confirms the pipe runs to the Akkas power station; Sputnik/Al-Jibawi confirm the field is the source. Both endpoints in Anbar governorate.

30 km is stated by the Al-Jibawi PDF ('extends for 30 km') and by the iraq-businessnews production article ('a 30-kilometre pipeline'), but I could NOT obtain a url_verifier-passing independent ref for the pipeline length: the Al-Jibawi PDF passes HTTP but the verifier cannot token-match compressed-PDF text, and iraq-businessnews.com returns HTTP 401 to both the verifier and WebFetch. Note also one 2022 pre-construction source (iraq-businessnews 'Work Begins', Aug 2022) gave 35 km. Value is defensible (30 km, as-completed) but left UNRESOLVED for a citable independent ref; do not fill the ref cell with the un-token-matchable PDF alone.

نفط الوسط = Midland Oil Company (MdOC), the state operator that brought Akkas online in March 2023. Named as operator by Zawya and iraqinews (both English). Refs name 'Midland Oil Company'; the GEM value is its Arabic form.

Field and infrastructure are state-owned; operator Midland Oil Company is a state company under the Iraq Ministry of Oil. Ministry-of-Oil ownership is inferential-but-standard for Iraqi state gas assets; no source names an explicit ownership share, so tier=medium.

routes.corridor_desc: ~30 km dry-gas line running roughly north within Al-Qaim district, Anbar, from the Akkas gas field (in the western desert ~30 km south of Al-Qaim, near the Syrian border) up to the 250 MW Akkas/Akaz gas power station adjacent to the Qaim 400kV substation. Corridor is bounded to a single district and ~30 km length, but the exact trace and the field CPF's precise coordinate are not sourced — medium-loose bound.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from independent sources: field = source (عكاز field ~30 km S of Al-Qaim, near the Syrian border — per Iraq Business News / Arabic press), power station = destination (attaqa: pipe feeds محطة كهرباء عكاس). END coordinate 34.3168N/41.1603E is the Akaz power station location reported by a Mapcarta feature and consistent with Al-Qaim (34.368N/41.090E) — given as APPROXIMATE. START coordinate 34.10N/41.10E is DERIVED (not directly sourced) from the described '~30 km south of Al-Qaim' field position, holding longitude near Al-Qaim's — flagged approximate; the field CPF's exact coordinate could not be sourced, so treat START as loose. No coordinate was fabricated from nothing; both trace to a named place. A routes-repo branch should refine the field-end coordinate before drawing geometry.

summary: P4401 Okaz (Akkas) Gas Pipeline is REAL and correctly classified as an operating gas-transmission line (SCOP, completed March 2023, 16″/30 km, Akkas field→Akkas power station, Anbar; operator Midland Oil Co). Caveats: GEM endpoints reversed (field stored as End, Start blank) and Capacity=75 / Diameter=16 trace only to the single Al-Jibawi source vs the widely-reported 60 MMcf/d throughput.
